## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Lóngwáng xiōngdì jīng* (T597) is a one-fascicle short *nāga* narrative translated by Zhī Qiān 支謙 ([支謙](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%94%AF%E8%AC%99)). The two *nāga*-king brothers Nanda 難陀 and Upananda 跋難陀 (or *Lóngwáng* 龍王 in plain Chinese paraphrase) attempt to obstruct the Buddha but are subdued by his disciple Maudgalyāyana.

**Abstract**

A brief disciplinary-mythological sūtra recounting the celebrated subjugation of the Nanda-Upananda *nāga* brothers — well-known from the Pāli *Mahāvagga* and from a wide spread of *Vinaya* and *Āgama* texts. Datable to Zhī Qiān's Wú-period activity (222–252 CE). Among the earliest Chinese versions of the episode.
